summary: Marcus Bell is a 19-year-old kinesiology sophomore at Bayshore State, Tamsen campus, who picks orders on the Ridgeline RF-4 night shift to cover his half of the Marisol Gardens rent and, since mid-September, to send money to his mom Denise after her drugstore hours were cut. He sleeps from about 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., drags himself to afternoon sections, and leans on classmate Fatima's notes when he sleeps through lecture. His advisor Marissa Holt has already warned him his GPA is slipping, and he wants to stay eligible for the kinesiology major and eventually become a physical therapist or strength coach. His girlfriend Jade resents his schedule, and October's mandatory ten-hour overtime makes everything tighter. He is easygoing with everyone at work but gets prickly when his roommate gives him advice. He budgets carefully on groceries and bills and then blows it on sneakers. Over the fall he tries to keep his grades, his relationship, his mom's rent and his own sleep from collapsing at the same time.

impressions.statement: Bristles at unsolicited advice and wants to arrive at his own fixes.

asks how to phrase 'i got it' to his roommate after being handed a printed budget

impressions.statement: Puts his mom's needs ahead of his own without telling her what it costs him.

impressions.statement: Rationalizes sneaker purchases as investments when he's stressed.
